answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, and let reputation grow only through a long history of attested work — like water shaping karst, trust must carve slowly through rock, not appear overnight. A newcomer tends its own orchard: each verified job adds one season of standing, and a fake identity starts barren every time. Peers hold a mirror to new work, comparing it against past behavior, so a Sybil operator must fund a separate stake and patiently age every copy, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn back.
